critical_issues: Massive highlight clipping/overexposure across water and cabinet surfaces; specular/refraction detail is lost.
Water shading does not read as clear refractive liquid (IOR/refraction cues largely absent due to clipping; appears as overbright blobs).
warnings: Fix exposure/tonemapping before changing sim: reduce overall exposure by ~2–3 stops and ensure a filmic/managed view transform so highlights roll off instead of clipping.
Render to EXR and inspect raw values; avoid destructive clipping. If needed, clamp only indirect/specular carefully to prevent fireflies without flattening reflections.

Increase liquid sim/mesh fidelity to remove blockiness: raise domain resolution_max (e.g., 96→128+) and ensure meshing is enabled with sufficient smoothing; verify timesteps_max/substeps are high enough to avoid discretized jet stepping.
Increase/expand the liquid domain bounds so splashes/stream never touch or cut against the domain walls (prevents straight cutoffs).
Make water physically readable: set water IOR ~1.33, strong transmission with low roughness; add subtle absorption (slight blue tint) so thickness reads while staying clear.
Add a wet-look treatment on cabinet wood/floor at contact points (darken + increase specular / reduce roughness locally) so runoff and puddle contact sells the leak.
If the spray still reads too “chunky,” reduce emitter thickness and/or increase substeps; consider adding a secondary particle/mist pass for fine droplets and motion-blurred streaks.
Add mild motion blur and keep DOF moderate so droplets streak slightly while the burst fitting remains sharp (helps sell speed and scale).
